findings.summary: The instrument table at line 181 reports 45 working, 1 starting, 4 queued, 19 held, 32 awaiting-upstream and 40 complete — 141 pointers — while the retained snapshot it sits beside records 140 pointers as working 42, starting 3, queued 5, held 18, awaiting-upstream 33, blocked 2 and complete 37; the table names no snapshot and omits the blocked phase, so the one figure set the five proposals rest on cannot be reconciled against the census JSON.

The session table's 'unloaded plans' column sums to 14 (5+3+2+2+1+1) while the note at line 121 states 11 plans, because two plans (a-landing-never-waits-on-a-shared-index and the-monitor-shows-the-work-it-watches) name more than one session; the column counts plan-session pairs under a header that reads as distinct plans.

The commit at a824e24ca3 replaced the figure 'review-refused 6 times in the log' on the stated premise that the retained window 'records a single row for that plan'; the retained log carries exactly 6 refused rows for r-20261114T222231293247 before 02:04Z and 25 passes naming it, so the removed figure was correct and the premise is contradicted by the artefact, while the replacement reads singular although two distinct requests were refused on that plan's review.

queued_pointers at line 68 re-derives the queued predicate that reckon/crew/admission/ordering.py:175 awaits_a_lane_slot already owns, and the plan's Deliverable required the census to read the queue through queued_placements and open_run_index.read_rows 'adding no third reader' — neither owner is called; the same function carries a dead branch at lines 75-76 ('... and False: pass'). The script is a run artefact rather than landed code, which is why this does not hold the node, but every figure in the fragment comes from it.

The census is tables only; no figure was committed under docs/figures/the-escape-lane-and-reviews-keep-pace/, which the run's own orientation_write_paths named as a topic directory, although the per-project table (eight projects, 342 implementable sections, 242 unloaded) is data one bar chart reads faster than a table.
